senses.sense_definition: A formal ceremonial gathering or reception held by an Indian ruler or by the British Raj.

examples.text: The viceroy attended the grand <w>durbar</w> held to mark the coronation of the new monarch.
Local dignitaries gathered at the <w>durbar</w> to pledge their allegiance to the prince.

traits.comment: Used primarily in South Asian historical contexts

senses.sense_definition: An audience hall or reception chamber in an Indian palace.

examples.text: Petitioners waited outside the great <w>durbar</w> hoping to be granted entry before the king.
The ornate pillars inside the <w>durbar</w> were carved from solid white marble.

traits.comment: Used primarily in South Asian contexts

senses.sense_definition: The official council or body of state advisers serving a ruler at an Indian court.

examples.text: The minister consulted the <w>durbar</w> before finalizing the terms of the regional peace treaty.
Several influential members of the royal <w>durbar</w> advised against raising land taxes.

traits.comment: Used primarily in South Asian historical contexts
